title: Miracle at Sea: Cruise Ship Pianist Rescued After Treading Water for 9 Hours in the Pacific
snippet: A Royal Caribbean pianist survived an incredible nine-hour ordeal floating in the Pacific Ocean before being spotted by Southern California fishermen nearly 20 miles off the coast.
content:
A musician aboard a Royal Caribbean cruise ship survived an extraordinary nine-hour ordeal in the open ocean after going overboard off the Southern California coast on Friday.

Sean Norton and Grant Garrett, two fishermen from Newport Beach, were heading home from a morning of marlin fishing near Catalina Island around noon when their boat's captain spotted a man floating in the water approximately 15 to 20 miles offshore.

A Desperate Rescue

After pulling the exhausted man onto their vessel, the crew discovered he was a pianist employed on the 14-deck cruise liner Ovation of the Seas. The survivor briefly lost consciousness after being brought aboard, but expressed immense gratitude once he awoke.

"The only thing he said to me was, 'Thank you. I thought I was gonna die,'" Norton recalled.

The fishing crew immediately broadcast an emergency maritime distress call, prompting a swift response from Newport Beach lifeguards. Newport Beach Fire Department Battalion Chief Adam Yacenda highlighted the remoteness of the site, describing the location as "pretty much in the middle of the ocean."

Royal Caribbean Responds

Authorities estimate the pianist went overboard roughly nine hours prior to his discovery. A spokesperson for Royal Caribbean Group confirmed the incident, stating that the company is providing support and assistance to the crew member during this time while maintaining his privacy.

Surviving an overboard incident in the open sea is remarkably rare. The miraculous rescue stands in stark contrast to a tragic event in September, when a passenger aboard the Carnival Panorama went missing off the coast of Mexico and was presumed dead after going overboard, underscoring just how fortunate the pianist was to be found alive.
